stdout_text:
Control your Eight Sleep Pod from the terminal

Usage:
  eightctl [command]

Available Commands:
  alarm       Manage alarms
  audio       Audio tracks and player
  autopilot   Autopilot settings
  away        Away mode (vacation)
  base        Adjustable base controls
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  daemon      Run schedule daemon from config file
  device      Device info and priming
  feats       List release features
  help        Help about any command
  household   Household info
  logout      Clear cached authentication token
  metrics     Sleep metrics and insights
  off         Turn pod off
  on          Turn pod on
  presence    Check if user is in bed
  schedule    Show the Autopilot (smart) schedule
  sleep       Sleep analytics commands
  status      Show device status
  temp        Set pod temperature (e.g., 68F, 20C, or heating level -100..100)
  tempmode    Temperature modes (nap, hot-flash, temp events)
  tracks      List audio tracks
  travel      Travel / jetlag endpoints
  version     Print version
  whoami      Show configured user ID

Flags:
      --client-id string       Eight Sleep client ID (optional; defaults to public app client)
      --client-secret string   Eight Sleep client secret (optional; defaults to public app client)
      --config string          config file (default ~/.config/eightctl/config.yaml)
      --email string           Eight Sleep account email
      --fields strings         output fields filter
  -h, --help                   help for eightctl
      --output string          output format: table|json|csv (default "table")
      --password string        Eight Sleep account password
      --quiet                  suppress config load message
      --timezone string        IANA timezone (e.g., America/New_York) or 'local' (default "local")
      --user-id string         Eight Sleep user ID
  -v, --verbose                verbose logging
      --version                version for eightctl

Use "eightctl [command] --help" for more information about a command.
change: a bare invocation is a usage error instead of help (C1)
